entities.summary: Khaneferre Sobekhotep IV was one of the most powerful Egyptian kings of the 13th Dynasty, who reigned for at least eight years. He was the son of King Sebekhotep V and succeeded his brother Neferhotep I as coregent before becoming the sole ruler. His reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Hyksos, a Semitic people who had conquered Egypt in the 17th century BCE. Sobekhotep IV launched a series of successful campaigns against the Hyksos, capturing several key cities, including Avaris and Saqqara. He also launched a naval campaign against the Hyksos in the Mediterranean, capturing several ships and territories. Despite these successes, Sobekhotep IV faced several challenges, including a rebellion by his brother Sihathor, who had become a powerful military leader. Sobekhotep IV eventually defeated Sihathor and solidified his control over Egypt. His legacy was marked by a series of impressive architectural projects, including the construction of a new capital at Avaris. Sobekhotep IV died in 1719 BCE, and his reign marked the beginning of a new era of Egyptian power and prosperity.
